title: Ways to organise ideas
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:48Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Ways to organise ideas
card: Ideas follow the order in which things happened or should happen. Recounts and instructions often use it, with words such as first, then and later.
Ideas show why something happened and what resulted. Words such as because, so and as a result link one idea to the next.
Ideas are sorted into groups and sub-groups. For example, a text on sharks might group them by size, then split each group into types.
A writer picks the way that suits the idea. A reader can spot the way by looking at how the ideas are linked.
draft.remember: Ask how the ideas are linked: by when, by why, or by group.

a.q: A text explains that heavy rain filled the creek, so the bridge flooded, and as a result the school closed. How are the ideas organised?
opts: By a taxonomy of weather types
a.why: Each idea leads to the next with so and as a result, which shows what caused what. It is not time order, because the links explain why things happened, not just when.
a.clue: Look at the linking words so and as a result.

b.q: A guide to Australian birds has a section on waterbirds. It splits them into ducks, herons and pelicans, then lists the types of duck. How is it organised?
opts: As a taxonomy of groups and sub-groups
As time order from first to last
As a recount of one day of birdwatching
b.why: The birds are sorted into a group, then split into smaller groups and types, which is a taxonomy. The list is not time order, even though the types are read one after another.
b.clue: Does the text sort things into bigger and smaller groups?

b.best: As a taxonomy of groups and sub-groups
